name: REINVENT
question: Does nightly or on-demand vardenafil after bilateral nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy improve unassisted erectile recovery after treatment withdrawal?

design.population: Men aged 18–64 years with preoperative IIEF-EF score at least 26 who were scheduled for bilateral nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Design, setting, and participants; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00492635, Study Design

verdictNote: Neither vardenafil schedule improved unassisted function after washout.
takeaway: Nightly vardenafil, on-demand vardenafil, and placebo were compared after bilateral nerve-sparing prostatectomy; neither active schedule significantly increased unassisted erectile recovery after the two-month washout, although on-demand dosing improved erectile function during treatment.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Montorsi F, Brock G, Lee J, et al. "Effect of Nightly versus On-Demand Vardenafil on Recovery of Erectile Function in Men Following Bilateral Nerve-Sparing Radical Prostatectomy." *Eur Urol.* 2008;54(4):924-931. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2008.06.083
reports.followUp: Nine months of randomized treatment, two-month washout, and optional two-month open-label treatment
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Design, setting, and participants

results.measure: Proportion with IIEF-EF score at least 22 after two-month washout
results.note: The abstract reports no statistically significant difference among groups; arm-specific rates, effect estimates, and the prespecified alpha are unavailable.

results.measure: IIEF-EF score and SEP3 success over nine-month treatment period
results.note: On-demand vardenafil produced higher IIEF-EF scores and SEP3 response rates than placebo; numerical results are unavailable in the abstract.

delivery.label: Treatment sequence
delivery.value: Nine months of double-blind nightly vardenafil, on-demand vardenafil, or placebo; two months of single-blind washout; optional two months of open-label treatment.
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Design, setting, and participants and Intervention
